mutations.because: skipping the active-job read lets the tombstone commit over a running job. The witness test seeds a running job keyed by slug and asserts outcome active-job with the seeded id; under this mutant the guard is gone, the tombstone commits, and the outcome equals requested instead — an assertion failure on the toEqual line. (Re-anchored by AR6: the active-job refusal now runs twice — once in the phase-1 check transaction, once re-taken under the phase-3 `for update` — so a mutant dropping one copy is still caught by the other and survives the witness; the anchor now spans both copies and drops both, which is the same fault end to end.)
command: requestCampaignDeletion refuses an active job and writes nothing

mutations.because: reading the job table by slug twice instead of slug + uuid makes a uuid-keyed running job invisible. The witness test seeds a running job whose campaign_id is the campaign uuid text and asserts outcome active-job with that id; under this mutant activeJobId finds nothing, the tombstone commits, and the outcome equals requested — the toEqual assertion fails. (Re-anchored by AR6: both copies of the refusal are keyed slug + uuid; the anchor now spans both and keys each by slug twice, which is the same fault end to end.)
command: requestCampaignDeletion sees a job keyed by the campaign uuid

mutations.because: dropping the tombstone read means a second DELETE on an already-tombstoned campaign re-inserts a deletion row. The witness test tombstones a campaign, calls a second time, and asserts outcome gone with exactly one deletion row; under this mutant the second call proceeds, the outcome is requested, and the count assertion fails. (Re-anchored by AR6: the tombstone read is duplicated by the precheck, so dropping one copy still answers gone; the anchor spans both copies and drops both — the same fault, and the only mutant the witness can see.)
command: requestCampaignDeletion on a tombstoned campaign answers gone and inserts nothing

mutations.because: disabling the team-scope authorisation lets a member delete an org-wide campaign. The witness test seeds an org-wide campaign and asserts outcome forbidden; under this mutant the check is skipped, the tombstone commits, and the outcome equals requested — the toEqual assertion fails. (Re-anchored by AR6: the refusal returns `as const` now; the mutation, its claim and its command are untouched.)
command: requestCampaignDeletion answers forbidden when mayDelete refuses the locked rows team and writes nothing

mutations.because: ignoring the requested grace hours makes every deletion insert at now() instead of now() + grace. The witness test passes graceHours 48 and asserts not_before - requested_at is 172800 seconds; under this mutant the difference is 0 and the assertion fails.
command: requestCampaignDeletion sets not_before from the grace hours

mutations.because: storing the slug as the deletion subject instead of the campaign uuid makes resolveCampaignForPurge throw or the subject assertion fail. The witness test asserts deletion.subject equals the campaign uuid; under this mutant subject is the slug and the toBe assertion fails.
command: requestCampaignDeletion tombstones the campaign and queues one deletion row

mutations.because: skipping the phase-3 active-job read lets the tombstone commit over a job that claimed the campaign in the gap between phase 1 and phase 3. The witness test plants a running job row inside the second transaction and asserts outcome active-job with that job id, deleted_at still null and no deletion row; under this mutant the guard is gone, the tombstone commits and the outcome equals requested — the toEqual assertion fails. Unlike mutations 0 and 1 this anchor covers only the phase-3 copy, isolating the re-check that runs under the re-taken for update lock.
command: requestCampaignDeletion refuses a job claimed only in the phase-3 gap at the tombstone

mutations.because: dropping the phase-3 tombstone read lets a second deletion proceed over a campaign a concurrent request tombstoned in the gap between phase 1 and phase 3. The witness test tombstones the campaign and inserts one deletion row inside the second transaction and asserts outcome gone with exactly one deletion row; under this mutant the tombstone runs again and a second row is inserted — the outcome is requested and both assertions fail. Unlike mutation 2 this anchor covers only the phase-3 copy, isolating the re-check under the re-taken for update lock.
command: requestCampaignDeletion answers gone for a concurrent tombstone in the phase-3 gap and leaves one deletion row
